Further context regarding using teleport for movement and stations for syncing:

The desync behavior can be seen here: The station rotates normally as seen by the line renderer while the player spins weirdly.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gDh2N7FB93U

This can be seen in this modification of Nestors NUMovement teleport movement system, which uses station for syncing.

https://github.com/iffn/NUMovementPlatformSyncModForVRChat

The current options aren't perfect, but at this point, the bigger risk seems to be future VRChat updates breaking these fragile systems.

I don't think this is necessary, if more advanced movement behaviour is required it should be up to the world to implement it and you can do so using stations, though being able to set a custom velocity for physbones is useful

@{62dee977f209dd5684d90d6c|full_name} I am not sure if you are really aware about limitation of stations and what I exactly want with this feature request.

Examples of two worlds I did:

https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_529dbcdc-a5af-48bb-bc6c-edb42d7ab3ec

This uses stations with a custom controller to move on the boats. If you try, you will see that it has some flaws - especially for desktop users. There are no walking animations and I have to reset the desktop rotation every 45° to avoid weird avatar twists. Crawl/crouch has to be implemented manually by switching between stations with different animations. VR with 3pt tracking can not move in real life, because the feet sticks somewhere at the station origin. GoGo Loco doesn't work too with this solution - this makes many players unhappy. But regarding to boat movement and physics, it's absolutely realistic.

https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_511d8efe-b233-4ffa-af92-846370aa0f47

The legacy version of the same world doesn't use stations, but moves the world instead. If you look on the water or boat movement, you will see that many of it is fake and doesn't look very realistic. Because of the technique, it's also limited to one single platform. And you cannot use rigidbodies, because the boat doesn't move. Optimizing/baking stuff is also impossible, because you can't set static toggles if a world has to move.

There are also other movement systems which uses different techniques - but no one of them works without flaws (and I tried many of them over a long range of time). Stations are definitely not a good solution to move on platforms in my opinion (but ok to simply play MMD or seating animations).

details:
Some players travels in a bus, on boats or spaceships and want to freely move on or in them. Currently, walking on platforms/transforms is difficult to solve.

**Feature Request**

Goal:

A feature which allows creators to build moving platforms and players can walk on them normally without any issues/restrictions. Creators can transfer players between platforms using trigger collider and any custom logic. A plattform can be part of a rigidbody or can be animated. Or the creator can use code to move a platform 2km back to origin (to avoid mesh jitter because of floating point accuracy). The creator is free to sync the position/rotation of this platform or not. All this affects not the players on the platform.

Solution:

`VRCPlayerApi.SetTransform(Transform platform)`

Takes a transform or null. As soon a transform is set, this will be synced to other players. Now, every player position, rotation, tracking data, velocity, teleport to, walking animation etc. is relative to this platform (aka "localPosition", "localRotation")

`VRCPlayerApi.GetTransform()`

Returns the current active transform or null.

`public override OnPlatformChanged(VRCPlayerApi player, Transform platform)`

Event allows to react on platform changes.

Gravity mode (World or Platform):

Gravity can be relative to world or relative to the platform (-transform.up). World should probably be default, but it should be configurable per platform.

PhysBones:

PhysBones could react relative to the platform or relative to the world. If a player walks inside of a bus, the PhysBones should probably react relative to the platform. If a player walks on a open top boat, the PhysBones should probably react relative to world (we expect crazy hair movement!). Platform should be the default. But world should be configurable per platform. PhysBones should also respect the gravity mode. PhysBones should also work for late joiners, independent how other players are orientated on their current platform.

Platform component:

If an additional component is required to mark a transform as a valid platform, this could be done by a VRCPlatform component. This can also contain flags to configure the settings mentioned:

`VRCPlatform.usePlatformGravity`

`VRCPlatform.applyWorldVelocityToPhysBones`

But this component should not limit the way how a platform can be used (boat, spaceship, zero gravity room, walk on walls, walk around planets - don't limit this).

**Actual Situation**

There are some workarounds, but no one works perfect. They tend to break easily on updates, which causes a lot of frustration.

Move the world instead the platform:

- this makes realistic physics impossible because the platform never moves

- moving the world looks "wrong" in some cases

- makes it immpossible to do some world optimization because it cant be static

Keep players in immobilized stations and create a custom controller to move them:

- many hacks required (specially for desktop, to reset the head rotation)

- permanent sync required per station

- no walking animations (build an custom animator impossible, because parameters can not be sent to a station-animator) 

- many avatar features does not work when players are permanently in immobilized stations

- remote players has an uncontrollable spin, if station exit/enter is used to reset the desktop head rotation (caused by mouse X)

Permanently teleport local player with the platform:

- works locally, but remote players lags always behind

Combination of teleporting, mobile station for local player and immobilized station for remote players:

- needs many hacks to get this working (teleporting player, enter back into station on every frame)

- permanent sync required per station

- breaks the VRC main menu

- remote players has an uncontrollable spin (because of permanent station exit/enter)

**Alternative Solutions**

VRCPlayerApi.TeleportTo could provide an additional "relativeTo" parameter, which takes a transform. This means, that the position/rotation provided to the method are "local" relative to this transform. This way, TeleportTo could be used to move players without lag from remotes perspective.

There is a way to send parameters to station animators. Custom walking/swimming/flying stations can take data needed to react on the environent (could also be 10-20 predefined "custom" parameters).

There is a way to deactivate the desktop head rotation in immobilized stations. The mouse x value is needed to turn a custom character controller. Currently this interfers with the desktop head turn.
title: Moving platform support - VRCPlayerApi.SetTransform(Transform platform)
